title: Recursive leaf-first recovery
story: I can finish incomplete work from its starting point without repeating completed effort.
jobStory: When related work is incomplete, I want to recover it from where it began, so I can finish the original task without repeating completed work.

scenarios.given: A user points to an incomplete root session with failed descendants.
scenarios.when: Recovery is started without the user supplying child IDs.
scenarios.then: Affected leaves finish first, their separate results propagate upward behind sibling barriers, and the root is reactivated after descendant work completes.

invalidation: A descendant is skipped despite failed work; sibling results are merged; a parent resumes before required siblings finish; completed work is repeated; or recovery stops without the root being reactivated.

items.description: Affected leaves finish first, their separate results propagate upward behind sibling barriers, and the root is reactivated after descendant work completes.

steps.description: Walk descendants to affected failed leaves without asking the user for child IDs.
Continue and finish each leaf’s work.
Prefer child-to-direct-parent wake with its own summary and brief note; otherwise collect output and pass it upward.
Preserve one attributable handoff per child.
Hold the parent until all required sibling recoveries complete.
Resolve children, resume each failed parent, and pass its result to its own parent until the root is reactivated.
Reuse completed/relaunched work and avoid duplicating the better existing investigation.
Account for timeout, connection, and provider-credit/credential failures under OpenCode controls; keep agents on the intended model.

for each leaf agent, i tell them 'continue and finish up'
we repeat until the root agent is reactivated

Reconciliation authority when messages, journals, or files conflict, including how to compare competing investigations.
Termination meaning (root running, root task done, or every descendant verified).
Model/depth defaults beyond explicit pinModel behavior and model inheritance for sessions not resumed by this run.
Data-model schema and persistence.
Whether core-restart emulation belongs in this plugin.
What retry, wait, model-switch, or stop policy applies to each failure class (timeout, network drop, provider credits/creds)?
notes: The inventory combines two exact quote fragments from the same source message.

Verified 2026-11-09: F-01-V1 acceptance passed on attempt 9 (root ses_e408c94f5ffewWj2xFGZsfC8z4) — an exact 1/2/4 tree of 7 sessions was built and interrupted, tree.recover resumed all 7 with rootReactivated=true, all 6 handoffs were delivered with parentResumed=true, and every original session finished idle_outcome=succeeded with a recovery:done journal entry (descendant count still exactly 7). Adversarial verification PASSed against the primary artifacts. Evidence: the private live-run capture, not published.

Implementation status (2026-11-01): tree.recover implements the recursive routine and NRR discovery; adversarial/live verification passed 2026-11-09 on attempt 9 (see the private live-run capture, not published).

Coordinator scope: The specified steps describe the desired outcome and handoff preference, but do not specify coordinator implementation mechanics. Do not infer a payload schema, summary length, or coordination mechanism from “summary” and “brief note.”

Termination condition: The specified stopping point is: the root is reactivated with all descendants successfully finished. What “successfully finished” proves, and whether root reactivation is sufficient or the root’s task must also be complete, remain open questions. Do not claim the workflow is verified until that termination contract is resolved and observable proof passes.

Why this was lost: The failed build translated the requested workflow into five primitives—`whoami`, `family`, `journal`, `handoff`, and `wake`—but never implemented the crawler, the sibling barrier, or upward result bubbling. Those primitives do not by themselves satisfy the leaf-first recovery feature.

Verified against the v2.1.2 source at ~/dev/opencode-src/packages/ on 2026-11-11: no origin column on session_v2, no source field on Session.Info, no session.create plugin hook (the whole session hook surface is prompt, context, compaction, generate, title, model.request, http.request, http.response, experimental.ws.*, retry at packages/plugin/src/effect/session.ts:139-151), and the session.created event carries metadata but no origin field (packages/schema/src/session-event.ts:48-66, metadata at :62).

`opencode run` writes no metadata (packages/cli/src/session-target.ts:60-68) and OpenChamber's default create writes none (ui/src/sync/session-actions.ts:1084-1088), so unlabelled roots are indistinguishable from user-started ones.
